name: Isolated Complex III Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain Complex III Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of isolated decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial disease such as exercise intolerance, muscle weakness, or multisystem involvement
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear or mitochondrial genes encoding complex III subunits or assembly factors
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or mitochondrial abnormalities
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biochemical evidence of isolated complex III deficiency plus compatible clinical features and genetic confirmation or supportive histological/biochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Isolated deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III activity
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by enzymatic assay in muscle or fibroblasts
searchTerms: low activity of mitochondrial complex III
complex III enzyme deficiency causing symptoms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe exercise intolerance with lactic acidosis
searchTerms: severe tiredness with lactic acid buildup
fatigue and muscle weakness on exertion
gradual weakness in upper legs and arms
failure to gain weight as baby
high lactate in blood or spinal fluid
eye muscle weakness or drooping eyelid
difficulty moving eyes or eyelid droop

rare.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities such as diabetes mellitus

laboratory: Isolated decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex III in muscle or fibroblasts
Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebral atrophy or basal ganglia abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial gene MT-CYB or nuclear genes such as BCS1L, TTC19
Mitochondrial DNA sequencing and nuclear gene panels for mitochondrial disorders
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial ultrastructure on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Decreased activity of complex I rather than complex III
Different genetic mutations affecting complex I subunits or assembly factors
Isolated deficiency of complex IV activity
Distinct clinical features such as Leigh syndrome more common
Broader mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiencies affecting multiple complexes

redFlags: Early onset progressive muscle weakness with lactic acidosis
Rapidly progressive cardiomyopathy in infancy or childhood
Multisystem involvement including neurological and hepatic dysfunction
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
